title: Engagement ignition: 45m facilitator playbook & escalation lanes
summary: A compact, timeboxed 45-minute QBR-style meeting template focused on driving renewal signals, surfacing operational risk, and creating fast decisions. Includes facilitator script, prep checklist, and escalation lanes for common risk scenarios.
content:
Purpose and intended use:
- Compact QBR / renewal checkpoint when the goal is to re-establish momentum, surface blockers, and commit to clear next steps in under 45 minutes. Good for mid-stage accounts (pilot → expansion) or exec-lite reviews.

Pre-reads (send 72h before):
- 1-page health snapshot (usage, errors, latency, cost trends) — attach as single slide or doc.
- Open action log from previous meeting (status + owner).
- Agenda + decision asks (explicit).

Participants (recommended):
- CSM (facilitator) — owns run of show and follow-ups
- Primary technical contact (engineer/owner) — to answer infra/latency questions
- Product sponsor / PM (customer) — roadmap alignment
- Finance or procurement (if renewal/commit decisions expected)
- Redwood SE or Solutions Eng backup (optional for escalation)

45m Run of show (timeboxed)
- 0:00–0:05 — Quick check-in & purpose (CSM)
  - Script: "Quick round: who’s on and one short success since we last spoke. Today we want to confirm health, resolve two blockers, and land 3 next steps."
  - Rule: 30s per participant to avoid drift.

- 0:05–0:14 — Health snapshot (CSM presents)
  - One slide: usage, latency percentiles, error rate, cost per 1k tokens, active routes, any SLA misses.
  - Facilitator prompts: "Call out anything surprising? Any recent incidents to highlight?"
  - Fallback: if metrics missing, call for an owner to supply post-meeting and mark as action.

- 0:14–0:27 — Top 2 opportunities & friction points (customer lead + CSM)
  - Format: 3 mins each for opportunity, 4 mins for friction/impact, 3 mins for alignment.
  - Prompts for customer: "If this works better what changes for your user/ops metrics?"
  - Evidence ask: request concrete success metric tied to adoption/ROI (e.g., 20% reduction in latency or X more LLM requests/day).

- 0:27–0:36 — Renewal signal & risk triage (CSM + finance/pm if present)
  - Explicit renewal ask (if applicable): "Based on current adoption, recommend moving to [reserved/dedicated] or keep hosted with optimizations."
  - Risk checklist (fast pass): adoption trend (↑ / ↓ by %), recent incidents, contract triggers, legal/security notes.
  - Decision prompt: "Do we need a commercial engagement this quarter? Yes/No. If Yes, who owns next step?"

- 0:36–0:42 — Escalation lanes & mitigation plan (CSM + SE)
  - Present triggers and immediate actions (see lanes below).
  - Ask for ownership and ETA.

- 0:42–0:45 — Decisions, next steps, parking lot (CSM)
  - Read back 3 commitments (owner + due date). Confirm follow-up cadence.

Facilitator script (concise cues):
- Opening: "We’ll keep to 45m—my job is to keep us on time and capture decisions. If something needs a deeper dive, we’ll add to the parking lot and assign."
- Health slide: "Two quick data points I want to call out..." then ask an open question: "Anything here that changed since your team last checked in?"
- When conversation drifts: "This is important—let’s park it and schedule a 30m deep dive. For this meeting, can we capture the ask and owner?"
- Closing: "I’ll send the recap within 24 hours with owners and due dates. Anything missing from our readout?"

Meeting prep checklist (CSM tasks, 72–24h before)
- [ ] Pull last 90-day usage and a 7-day trend (token volumes, top routes) — owner: CSM / metrics analyst
- [ ] Compile top 3 errors or incidents with current status — owner: SRE contact
- [ ] Get finance note: spend vs. forecast and any overage risk — owner: CSM or finance partnership
- [ ] Confirm attendees and decision-makers; escalate required attendees 48h prior — owner: CSM
- [ ] Upload single-slide health snapshot to meeting invite — owner: CSM
- [ ] Draft 1 recommended commercial/technical action (if renewal window <90 days) — owner: CSM

Decision log (use during meeting):
- Decision 1: [short statement] — Owner: [name] — Due: [YYYY-MM-DD]
- Decision 2: [short statement] — Owner: [name] — Due: [YYYY-MM-DD]
- Note: keep decisions atomic and measurable.

Escalation lanes (fast reference)
- Lane A — Production SLA / severe latency or errors (>5% error rate or P95 > 3x baseline)
  - Immediate: Triage call with customer SRE + Redwood SRE within 2 hours.
  - Owner: Redwood SRE oncall + CSM to coordinate.
  - Expected outcome in 24h: mitigation plan + temporary routing/fallback.
  - Escalate to Platform Eng lead if no mitigation within 24–48h.

- Lane B — Security / compliance flags (exposure, data residency concerns)
  - Immediate: Pause non-critical changes; open security incident channel and notify security@redwood.
  - Owner: CSM + Security PM.
  - Expected outcome in 48h: initial triage and remediation plan.

- Lane C — Commercial / contract risk (renewal likely to decline, budget cut)
  - Immediate: Align on next internal sync: CSM + AE + finance within 48h.
  - Owner: AE (commercial), CSM (operational).
  - Play: propose 30/60/90 day plan with milestones and executive sponsor outreach.

- Lane D — Feature gap blocking key use case (product dependency)
  - Immediate: Capture minimal repro, user impact, and timeline ask.
  - Owner: Product sponsor + Solutions Eng.
  - Escalate to product triage board if impact = high and ROI justifies priority.

Common meeting anti-patterns (and How to avoid)
- Anti-pattern: Deep technical debugging in the QBR. Fix: Park the item; schedule a 30–60m deep-dive with SEs.
- Anti-pattern: No decision owners. Fix: Force assign at the moment of the decision and confirm date.
- Anti-pattern: Metrics not trusted/old. Fix: Mark metrics as "TBC" and assign a data owner to validate within 48h.

Quick templates to paste in invite/outcome email:
- Invite blurb (72h): "Goal: 45m momentum checkpoint — confirm product health, decide on top 1–2 commercial/technical actions, and agree owners. Please review attached health snapshot and open actions before we meet."
- Outcome blurb (24h): "Thanks — summary: decisions taken, owners and due dates below. Actions: [list]. Next touch: [date/time]. If you need adjustments, reply to this thread by EOD."

Notes to self / CSM tips:
- If the customer asks for a new feature roadmap item, ask for one concrete success metric tied to adoption before promising prioritization.
- Keep a running parking lot doc during the call; it helps show progress and preserves trust.
- When in doubt, escalate early — especially for security and SLA items.

Appendix: Useful links to attach in pre-read
- One-click health snapshot template: https://confluence.redwood/health-snapshot-template
- Renewal readiness checklist (commercial): CONFLUENCE-RENEWAL-2024
- Incident playbook (SRE): CONFLUENCE-SRE-INCIDENTS

End of document.

(Version notes: first draft, focused on compact, decision-oriented meetings. Intend to iterate based on CSM feedback after 3 customer runs.)
